question: The vocal performance Kathakali has traditionally been performed in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskritised Malayalam.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kathakali:-**

 
 
• **Kathakali is a form of classical Indian dance-drama which originated in the present-day state of Kerala during the 17th century and has developed over the years. **
 
• It is performed by elaborately costumed male artists who tell stories through their facial expressions, hand gestures, and stylized body movements.
 
• **The art form is traditionally performed in Sanskrit-based Malayalam, although modern performances may include other languages.**
 
• The vocal performance of Kathakali is known as geet or sopanam. It is performed by a group of trained singers who are positioned off-stage and accompany the dancers with their singing.
 
• The singers sing the lyrics of the play, which are in the form of verses that are metered and lyrical.
 
• **The singing is synchronized with the dance-acting on the stage, and the vocalists help to set the context and express the inner state of the character by modulating their voice.**
 
• For example, anger is expressed by the use of a sharp high voice and pleading is expressed by the use of a sad tone. Music is also central to a Kathakali performance. It sets the mood and triggers emotions resonant with the nature of the scene.
